title: Two lamps in the rain
hookLine: three strangers squeeze into one dark shelter in the rain, someone unseen presses in, and each lights a lamp with a song
carry: light the lamp, and god is already near
tomorrow: God appears in the sky. what's the old man's first worry?

cards: Rain, hard and sudden, at night, in a town called Tirukkovalur. A wandering singer ducks into a tiny covered passage, room enough for one to lie down. A second soaked stranger asks to come in.
Room for one to lie, the first says, means room for two to sit. A third arrives. Room for two to sit means room for three to stand.
So three strangers stand shoulder to shoulder in the dark, dripping. Then the space gets tighter, as if a fourth body has pressed in among them. Nobody came through the door.
That's the story the Sri Vaishnava tradition tells about how three of the Alvar hymns began.

teach.b: The three, the story goes, were Poygai, Bhutam and Pey. Crammed in the dark with someone unseen, they don't panic or push. Each one lights a lamp, and the lamps are songs.

teach.h: A LAMP AS BIG AS THE WORLD.
teach.b: Poygai sings a lamp on the scale of the world: the earth for the bowl, the ocean for the oil, the blazing sun for the flame, offered at the feet of the Lord.

Bhutam answers with a lamp on the scale of a heart: love for the bowl, longing for the oil, a mind melting with joy for the wick, lit as a lamp of knowing. In that double light, Pey sings what he sees.

The fourth one, pressing in, is Vishnu, with Lakshmi, the goddess of fortune, beside him. I have seen, he sings, and he names it: the goddess, a golden form, a color like the blazing sun, the wheel, the conch.
Sri Vaishnavas read the story as God wanting to be among his devotees, standing there the whole time. And it shows why a lamp comes first in so much Hindu worship.
Many families light a diya at dusk; at the aarti a flame is waved before the deity.

teach.h: LIGHT THE LAMP. GOD IS NEAR.
teach.b: The lamp is an offering, and it's how you see who's there: one lamp outside, one of love inside. Each Alvar's verses became a linked hymn, an antadi.

how: Sri Vaishnavas tell the story of the three Alvars at Tirukkovalur, and their three linked hymns are recited as part of the collection of Alvar songs in temples and homes.

o: Tamil hymns sung to Vishnu by the poet-saints
Sanskrit prayers chanted only by temple priests
court poems written to praise the Tamil kings

games.q: three lamps in the rain: tap the pairs.
p: the earth for a bowl, the sun for a flame
love for a bowl, a melting mind for a wick
a verse's last word starts the next

s: the three singers pushed the fourth out of the shelter
they lit lamps with songs instead, and saw Vishnu with Lakshmi among them.
one lamp was as big as the world, one as close as feeling
Poygai's lamp is earth, ocean and sun; Bhutam's is love, longing and a melting mind.
at the aarti, a flame is waved before the deity
the lamp is an offering, and it lights up the one you came to see, like the Alvars' two lamps.

games.q: you're standing in a tiny dark shelter with two strangers. the space gets tighter, as if someone else has pressed in. what do you do?
o: push toward the door and get out.
shout until whoever it is leaves.
light a lamp, and see who's there.
games.why: in the story the three Alvars each light a lamp with a song, and in that light Pey sees Vishnu with Lakshmi, standing among them.

practice: Light two lamps. First the wide one: let your attention open to everything at once, the floor holding you, the air, the sky above the roof.
Then the close one: bring to mind someone or something you love, and let that warmth fill the chest like oil in a small bowl.
Sit in both kinds of light and see who seems near; if you pray, let the one you pray to be the one who's near.

wordCard.voice: The Alvar hymns. Today, three singers in one dark shelter, two lamps, and a fourth who was already there.

orig.note: Tamil: the linked verse form of these hymns, each verse beginning with the last word of the one before.

carryVoice: Your line: light the lamp, and God is already near. They made room in the dark, and someone was already there. Go gently.
